job.title: Fractional CFO
job.description:
Interim Chief Financial Officer


Interim Chief Financial Officer Lead finance through a period of fast growth at a $20M energy company in the New York metro.

Location  New York metro Schedule  Hybrid Function  Finance Engagement  Interim


The role

Our client is growing quickly, and the business has become more complex than its finance function was built to

handle. The company needs an interim CFO who can come in right away, take ownership of cash and liquidity, and give the CEO clear financial insight for decisions that can’t wait. You’ll work closely with the CEO, senior leadership and the company’s third-party accounting firm. The assignment is hands-on. You’ll assess what’s in place, then set the priorities that bring structure and discipline to finance ahead of the company’s next stage.


The organization

Our client is an energy company in the New York metro with about $20M in revenue and strong growth. It relies on a third-party accounting firm for day-to-day accounting. This is an interim engagement.


What you'll do

  • Cash and liquidity
  • Take ownership of cash flow management and short-term liquidity planning Build and maintain a short-term cash forecast that identifies funding needs
  • Evaluate working capital needs in light of the company’s growth Give leadership early visibility into cash needs and risks
  • Reporting and close
  • Review the balance sheet and income statement for accuracy, completeness and appropriate accounting treatment, and drive remediation of gaps
  • Partner with the accounting firm to deliver a faster, more efficient monthly close
  • Leadership
  • Serve as strategic financial partner to the CEO and senior leadership team Find opportunities to improve profitability and overall financial performance


What we're looking for

  • CFO or senior finance executive experience in fast-growing, entrepreneurial companies
  • Strong cash flow, liquidity and working capital management skills
  • Experience improving financial reporting and accelerating the monthly close
  • Deep balance sheet and P\&L expertise
  • Experience working with outsourced or third-party accounting providers
  • A record of professionalizing a finance function as a company grows
  • Strong executive presence and communication skills
  • A hands-on approach, with comfort operating on incomplete information and tight timelines


How to apply

This is a confidential search managed by Lyneer Search Group. To talk about the role, or to recommend someone

who should hear about it, contact our team. Every conversation stays between us.

resume@lyneersearch.com


Evaluated through the Lyneer Executive Search Strategy™

Every candidate is assessed across 4 dimensions: technical skill, leadership capability, cultural alignment and long-term growth potential.

job.title: Manager, Tax Information Reporting
job.description:
Tax Reporting Lead Analyst, AVP/VP

 

Wealth management · Private wealth


Location New Jersey 

Schedule Hybrid, 3 days in office 

Function Tax operations

Line NRA withholding and reporting


The opportunity

A private wealth management firm in New Jersey is hiring a tax reporting lead analyst for its tax operations team. You'd be the firm's technical expert on nonresident alien withholding and information reporting, with primary ownership of Forms 1042 and 1042-S. It's a replacement hire.


What you'll own

  • Own the Form 1042-S process end to end: data validation, reconciliation, filing, corrections and amendments.
  • Reconcile Form 1042 to Forms 1042-S, withholding liabilities, federal tax deposits and IRS account transcripts, and resolve discrepancies.
  • Review Forms W-8 for validity, recipient status, withholding rates and treaty eligibility.
  • Advise on the Chapter 3 and FATCA treatment of corporate actions, income distributions and cross-border transactions.
  • Track regulatory changes and work with operations and technology on system enhancements, testing and automation.
  • Support year-end reporting on Forms 1099, 1099-R and 5498.


What the firm is looking for

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business or taxation, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 5 to 7+ years of tax information reporting, with substantial hands-on Forms 1042 and 1042-S work.
  • Advanced knowledge of Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 (FATCA), Forms W-8, and treaty and withholding rules, with the judgment to research and resolve complex issues on your own.
  • Form 1042 reconciliation and IRS account transcript analysis.
  • Advanced Excel, and the ability to explain complex tax issues to business and technology partners.
  • Preferred: controls, audit or regulatory exam support; FIS Wall Street Concepts or Global Plus; Forms 1099 reporting; SIFMA involvement.

job.title: Senior Investment Accountant

job.title: Financial Wealth Planner
job.description:
Wealth Planner

The Wealth Planner prepares estate and wealth planning analyses, including estate flowcharts, financial models, planning materials, and technical assessments to support high-net-worth client objectives. This role serves as a technical resource to internal teams, providing expertise, tools, and guidance to inform client-focused wealth planning strategies.

 

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Wealth Planning & Analysis                                                 

  • Develop estate and wealth transfer strategies, including creating flowcharts, illustrations, summaries, and related planning materials.
  • Review and analyze estate planning documents to identify opportunities and support client objectives.
  • Build financial models and impact analyses using NaviPlan, Microsoft Excel, and other tools.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to understand objectives, incorporate insights, and deliver high-quality planning recommendations.

 

Internal Technical Resource                                               

  • Provide technical guidance to client teams during planning and meeting preparation.
  • Review work from associates and integrate feedback from Managing Directors and Client Service Teams.
  • Research and respond to estate and financial planning questions.
  • Stay current on tax, legislative, and industry developments.

 

Tools, Templates & Education                                               

  • Develop and maintain planning templates, reports, and analyses.
  • Contribute to internal technical content, training materials, and educational resources.

 

Administrative, Professional Development & Other Duties                      

  • Handle administrative tasks, attend internal meetings, and participate in ongoing training.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as needed to support the firm and client teams.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree and an advanced degree in relevant field or professional designation (such as CFP, CPA, CPWA), required.
  • 3+ years of experience in wealth, estate, or tax planning; experience with ultra-high-net-worth individuals and multi-generational families preferred but not required.
  • Strong analytical and technical skills, with the ability to interpret complex estate documents, financial statements, and tax returns.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office; experience with NaviPlan or similar financial planning software preferred.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex strategies clearly and client-readily.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, discretion, and respect for confidential matters.
  • Positive, collaborative mindset with a strong work ethic.

job.title: Senior Tax Accountant
job.description:
Senior Tax Accountant

Client, a premier individual wealth management firm, is hiring a Senior Tax Accountant for its suburban Philadelphia office.


This senior-level role will prepare and review complex tax returns, coordinate tax compliance for high-net-worth clients and related entities, and serve as a client-facing resource while partnering with Wealth Advisors, Trust Officers, Operations, and other internal teams to deliver coordinated client service. The position requires strong federal, state, local, and fiduciary tax knowledge; sound judgment; excellent analytical skills; and the ability to manage competing deadlines in a high-touch wealth management environment. 


Responsibilities

  • Prepare and review complex federal, state, and local tax returns, including individual income tax returns (Form 1040), gift tax returns (Form 709), partnership returns (Form 1065), private foundation returns (Form 990-PF), and fiduciary income tax returns for trusts and estates (Form 1041). 
  • Review assigned returns and supporting workpapers for technical accuracy, completeness, consistency with source documents, and compliance with department procedures. 
  • Manage the tax compliance process for a portfolio of high-net-worth clients, including gathering financial information, coordinating deliverables, communicating with clients, and addressing tax-related inquiries. 
  • Conduct tax research on complex tax issues and provide recommendations to management and clients 
  • Coordinate tax engagement workflows and monitor filing deadlines to ensure timely completion of client deliverables. 
  • Assist in the preparation of estimated tax payments and extensions. 
  • Collaborate with Wealth Advisors, Trust Officers, and Operations teams to ensure accurate and timely tax reporting and client service. 
  • Participate in client meetings and communicate tax matters and planning recommendations in collaboration with Wealth Advisors and Tax Management. 
  • Assist with tax notices, audits, and other tax authority inquiries. 
  • Conduct tax research on complex federal and state issues and provide well-supported recommendations to Tax Management and clients. Stay current with changes in tax laws and regulations and assess their impact on the company and its clients. 

 

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting. 
  • Master's degree in Taxation preferred. 
  • 8-12 years of experience in public accounting, private client tax, fiduciary tax, and/or wealth management tax services. 
  • CPA or EA designation preferred; CFP designation is a plus.
  • Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local tax laws and regulations, with significant experience preparing and reviewing Forms 1040, 709, 1065, 990-PF, and 1041. 
  • Experience with CCH Axcess Tax is strongly preferred. Experience with CCH Scan, Bloomberg Tax/BNA Tax Planner, CCH AnswerConnect, or Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Trust Tax is a plus.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deadlines. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex tax matters clearly to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. 
  • Ability to work in the office three days per week.

job.title: Senior Manager, Technical Accounting
job.description:
VP of Technical Accounting Advisory


To complement its existing Transaction Advisory Services offering, our client is continuing to grow its Technical Accounting Advisory practice. This team provides commercially focused technical accounting advice across the entire deal continuum, from the assessment of pre deal accounting complexities to post close financial reporting. The team provides specialist accounting advice to clients across a range of areas, often working as part of cross-functional teams including Transaction Advisory Services, Tax and Valuations.


We are seeking a high-caliber individual looking to build on their current technical knowledge and commercial experience to take on a leadership role within this team. The individual will be responsible for driving the growth an existing book of work with a clear career progression path to Director and on to Managing Director on an accelerated basis.


Day-to-day Responsibilities

  • Help identify efficient and effective solutions to technical accounting and transaction issues and deliver these solutions to our clients
  • Execute and lead technical accounting workstreams, including preparation and review of deliverables, including technical memos, supporting workbooks, and financial statement disclosures
  • Assessing the appropriate treatment for complex or judgemental accounting issues, e.g., revenue recognition, financial instruments, share-based payments, Fresh Start Accounting, GAAP conversions etc.
  • Work on a collaborative basis across our practice
  • Consistently deliver excellent client service
  • Contribute on a proactive basis to the leadership and direction of our group through the on-going development of internal and external relationships
  • Ability to understand the problems and issues in achieving the required client outcomes and to be able to research the potential solutions autonomously and through consultation with colleagues
  • Assist with various business development initiatives
  • Bachelor’s in Accounting, Economics, Finance or related discipline
  • CPA Certification Required
  • Minimum 5 years US GAAP technical accounting experience (in particular ASC 805, ASC 606, ASC 718, ASC 815, ASC 470)
  • ASC 852 Bankruptcy experience would be a positive but is not mandatory
  • Public accounting experience
  • Experience in writing technical accounting memorandums
  • Key interest in M&A advisory; accounting due diligence; purchase price allocations; fresh start accounting; financial instruments

Essential Traits

  • Strong interpersonal, communication, marketing, sales and organizational skills
  • High proficiency in the use Microsoft Office, with focus on Excel, PowerPoint and Word
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills that help represent diverse communities
  • Experience working with diverse teams

job.title: Client Advisor
job.description:
Client Advisor

 

The Client Advisor role is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative team of dedicated professionals that service this firm’s ultra-high net worth clients. The Client Advisor is responsible for developing and maintaining client relationships through proactive client communication and the coordinated delivery of services to individuals, families, trusts, and foundations. The Client Advisor acts internally as a liaison between Senior Client Advisors and all other service areas of the organization, such as Tax and Financial Planning, Investments, Legacy Planning and Trust Administration, Alternative Asset Management, Philanthropic Advisory, Real Estate and Insurance Advisory.


Responsibilities:


Client Service

·        Communicate with clients and their advisors regularly. Provide timely and thorough response.

·        Attend client meetings, document issues discussed and coordinate follow up.

·        Oversee preparation of client meeting materials. Create custom reports proactively and as requested.

·        Document client information and communications in Salesforce.


Account Administration

·        Oversee account opening and closing procedures and review related documents.

·        Oversee account transactions and reporting.

·        Review and be comfortable with client wills, trusts and governing documents and their application to client account administration. Establish necessary automated reminders and follow through.

·        Coordinate with fiduciary counsel as needed to ensure administration is in accordance with governing documents

·        Prepare Annual Relationship Reviews and assure that all accounts comply with all regulatory requirements.

 

Investment Management

·        Assist the Senior Client Advisor in investment management activities including implementing investment objectives, rebalancing accounts, executing trades, monitoring asset allocation and investment performance, and overseeing investment transition

·        Monitor daily internal reports and work with account team to resolve any issues, such as overdrafts

·        Coordinate client requests for funds including regular disbursements

·        Prepare asset allocation simulation modeling.

 

Trust Administration

·        Prepare initial and annual trust reviews and requests for all discretionary distributions from trusts and for all special investments in trust

·        Make required distributions from trusts and foundation

·        Coordinate annual unitrust payments and private foundation grant payments with tax department

·        Process gifts to charity and family. Prepare and send Crummey letters as appropriate

·        Coordinate with tax department (or clients outside tax preparers) on reporting gifts to, and use of GST exemption on gift tax returns for, irrevocable trusts

·        Prepare reports to Trust Builder for irrevocable insurance trusts (ILITs), make transfers to ILITs as required and pay life insurance premiums

·        Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 

Qualifications:

 

·        Bachelors degree in a relevant field and 7 to 10 years of related business experience. Masters preferred. Excellent writing and presentation skills

·        Demonstrated leadership and teamwork qualities

·        Ability to organize, complete multiple tasks within deadlines and complete accuracy

·        Series 7, Series 63 license desired with two years of Cannon Trust School or equivalent. CTFA, CFP or CFA is a plus

·        Ideally, proficient in Microsoft Office Suite - Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, and Salesforce.

job.title: Managing Director
job.description:
Managing Director


Position Overview

This opportunity is designed for an established financial services leader who wants the entrepreneurial upside of building and leading a significant organization, while leveraging an existing platform with the infrastructure, resources, specialists, and support necessary to scale. The MD will have the ability to recruit and develop their own organization while leveraging company's broader capabilities to help advisors expand their practices and serve clients across insurance, retirement, investments, and financial planning.

We are looking for a leader who can make an immediate impact while also seeing the long-term opportunity to build a substantial business and leadership legacy.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Recruit and attract full-time financial professionals and advisors.
  • Build, lead, and grow a productive financial services organization.
  • Coach and develop both new and experienced advisors.
  • Drive advisor productivity, professional development, retention, and overall organizational growth.
  • Establish clear expectations and accountability around activity and results.
  • Identify and develop future managers and leaders within the organization.
  • Drive growth across life insurance, annuity, retirement, and broader financial planning opportunities.
  • Help advisors develop sustainable client acquisition strategies and repeatable business-development systems.
  • Collaborate with company leadership, recruiting, training, operations, and our broader ecosystem of specialists.
  • Build and maintain a culture centered on growth, professionalism, relationships, service, and performance.
  • Represent company professionally within the financial services industry and marketplace.


Experience & Qualifications

  • Minimum of 3 years of demonstrated success in a financial services management or leadership role.
  • Candidates should ideally come from the life insurance, retirement planning, financial advisor, wealth management, or related financial services distribution environment.
  • Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain financial professionals.
  • Experience leading a team, agency, office, market, or advisor organization.
  • Strong understanding of life insurance and retirement strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive advisor productivity and organizational growth.
  • Experience coaching and developing advisors at different stages of their careers.
  • Track record of measurable recruiting, retention, and/or production results.
  • Experience identifying and developing future managers and leaders is highly desirable.
  • Exposure to investments, advisory business, and AUM is preferred but not required.


﻿Licensing & Credentials

  • Active Life & Health insurance license required.
  • Series 65, Series 7 & 66, or an applicable professional designation that satisfies IAR qualification requirements is preferred, but not required.
  • Existing investment advisory and AUM experience is considered a strong plus given client's RIA platform.
  • Additional industry licenses, professional designations, and credentials are viewed favorably.

job.title: Senior Wealth Strategist
job.description:
Managing Director & Senior Wealth Strategist

 

POSITION SUMMARY 

As a key member of the Family Office Services Team, the Managing Director & Senior Wealth Strategist is responsible for producing and reviewing complex estate and wealth planning deliverables, identifying and developing proactive observations and recommendations, and interpreting complex estate planning documents and financial information. Additionally, the role serves as a key estate planning technical resource for the firm, collaborating with Managing Directors and the client team to prepare for and attend client meetings. The role of the Managing Director & Senior Wealth Strategist also involves providing firm-wide support on tax and estate planning issues, writing and publishing expert articles, maintaining educational materials, and offering subject matter expertise and training to internal associates.

 

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Produces and performs review of complex client estate and wealth planning deliverables        

  • Reviews estate flowcharts and prepares/reviews other complex estate planning technical deliverables.
  • Develops and reviews observations and recommendations relative to specific planning issues and strategies with an eye toward proactive opportunities.
  • Develops and reviews technical, complex and comprehensive plans focused on wealth transfer and estate planning ensuring that objectives/observations and information from Managing Directors, Client Service Associates and other members of the broader client cell team are incorporated into the Comprehensive Plan.
  • Reviews, analyzes and summarizes sophisticated estate planning documents.
  • Provides guidance for Wealth Strategist in oversight of the administration of various family entities and comprehensive services related to maintaining client’s family office needs.
  • Develops and maintains, with demonstrated excellence, templates for various estate planning reports, analysis and deliverables.
  • Anticipates client questions.

 

Serves as an estate planning technical resource to the Managing Directors in preparing for client meeting and in attending meetings

  • Collaborates with Managing Director and internal client cell team on specific client deliverables, general technical matters and proactive strategies related to various client and internal associate needs.
  • Demonstrates excellence in serving as an estate planning technical resource in client or advisor meetings.
  • Participates in client/prospect/advisor meetings as needed.
  • Participates in feedback/debrief meetings and takes a active approach to continuous improvement.

 

Serves as a technical resource for and to the firm                       

  • Provides support, clarity and answers to technical issues/questions related to tax and estate planning.
  • Researches, writes, and publishes high-quality articles on complex wealth transfer topics for professional journals, industry publications, and online platforms. Ensure all content is accurate, well-researched, and adheres to the highest standards of legal writing.
  • Meets/communicates regularly with outside advisors for technical estate planning discussions and review, with developed beneficial relationships with outside advisors.
  • Reviews, develops and maintains FOS technical materials and educational pieces related to estate and wealth planning.
  • Reviews or creates and maintains estate planning related technical education summaries and materials.
  • Provides subject matter expertise and training opportunities to internal associates.
  • Performs other duties as assigned                                        

 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • College degree with a postgraduate degree of JD, L.L.M or MST and/or a professional designation of CPA, CFP® and/or CPWA®  and 10 years relevant experience in estate and tax planning and/or fiduciary and trust planning and administration.
  • Must possess a foundation of technical and business expertise with prior experience in strategic wealth planning for high-net-worth individuals and multi-generational families.
  • Must have in-depth knowledge of current legislative and case law changes and other technical developments in the estate planning area.
  • Must have strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret/analyze estate planning documents, financial statements and tax returns with strong attention to detail.
  • Must have demonstrated excellence in written and verbal communication skills as frequent author and presenter of complex estate planning strategies.
  • Must have excellent computer skills in Excel with ability to build Excel worksheets relative to complex planning strategies preferred.
  • Must have ability to explain complex estate planning strategies in a client friendly manner.
  • Must have a professional demeanor with the utmost respect for confidential matters.
  • Must be able to work independently and in a team environment.
  • Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong interpersonal skills.
  • Must be detail oriented with excellent organizational skills.
  • Must have ability to multi-task.
  • Must have ability to work in a fast paced environment.
  • Must have strong work ethic with a positive attitude.

 

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Limited travel as business needs necessitates
  • Long periods of sitting utilizing a computer
  • 100% onsite

job.title: Reinsurance Finance Director
job.description:
Finance Director, Reinsurance

Lead the finance review of the MGA programs our client writes and renews, and give senior leadership an independent view of whether each one holds up.


  • Industry: Insurance: MGA program business and reinsurance
  • Function: Finance
  • Direct report: Senior Reinsurance Accountant
  • Working model: Hybrid, up to 2 days per week in office


The role

This role provides financial oversight across our client's MGA program business and reinsurance portfolio. You'll lead the finance review of new and existing programs and decide whether each is financially sound, appropriately collateralized, accurately forecast, and consistent with the company's risk appetite and strategic objectives.

Most of the work is cross-functional. You'll work with Finance, Treasury, Underwriting, Reinsurance, Program Management, Risk, Legal, Accounting, Claims, and senior leadership, testing program economics, financial assumptions, collateral sufficiency, profitability, and emerging financial risks, then bringing independent recommendations to executive management. You'll also oversee the preparation and governance of quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral monitoring, and financial forecasting.


The organization

Our client is an insurance group writing MGA and program business, supported by a reinsurance portfolio and subject to US and international regulatory obligations. Finance confirms a program is financially ready before it launches, and its analysis goes to senior leadership, Risk Committees, Reinsurance Committees, and the Board.


What you'll do

Program evaluation and onboarding

  • Lead the finance workstream for evaluating and onboarding new and renewed MGA and program business.
  • Review program economics: premium projections, commissions, fees, taxes, reinsurance structures, expenses, collateral requirements, profitability, and financial assumptions.
  • Perform financial due diligence on profitability, capital utilization, liquidity, cash flow, collateral exposure, and downside scenarios.
  • Work with Underwriting, Reinsurance, Treasury, Accounting, Program Management, Legal, Risk, FP&A, and Claims to confirm financial readiness before a program launches.

Collateral and counterparty risk

  • Oversee collateral governance, including letters of credit, trust accounts, funds withheld arrangements, recoverables, and collateral sufficiency.
  • Monitor reinsurer financial strength, counterparty credit risk, recoverability, and collateral adequacy, and identify emerging financial risks.

Reporting and governance

  • Prepare and review Schedule F reporting, quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral reporting, cash flow forecasts, and executive management presentations.
  • Develop executive reporting, dashboards, profitability analysis, and governance materials for senior leadership, Risk Committees, Reinsurance Committees, and the Board.
  • Evaluate financial performance, forecast accuracy, program profitability, and emerging trends, and recommend improvements and corrective actions.
  • Maintain the governance frameworks, documentation standards, financial controls, and finance review processes behind program oversight.

Leadership

  • Supervise and develop the Senior Reinsurance Accountant, who is responsible for quarterly reinsurance reporting, collateral reporting, and forecasting.
  • Give senior leadership strategic financial guidance and independent recommendations on program readiness, collateral exposure, profitability, and financial risk.
  • Keep improving financial reporting, collateral monitoring, forecasting processes, and governance practices.

Regulatory obligations

You'll maintain compliance with every applicable US or international statutory and regulatory obligation the role carries, including those arising from:

  • The prudent management of the business.
  • Due regard for the interests of customers.
  • Rules on sanctions and financial crime.
  • Regulatory requirements and local licensing restrictions.
  • The Group's whistleblowing procedures, which you'll promote and follow, and guide your reports on.
  • Where applicable, the company's Consumer Duty principles, to deliver good outcomes for retail customers.


What we're looking for

Skills

  • Strong knowledge of insurance finance, reinsurance, MGA and program business, collateral management, and financial reporting.
  • Substantial experience evaluating program economics, profitability, budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling, and business cases.
  • A strong understanding of reinsurance structures, recoverables, collateral arrangements, letters of credit, trust agreements, and ceded balances.
  • Experience analyzing financial statements, capital adequacy, liquidity, credit quality, and counterparty financial strength.
  • Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and financial modeling skills, and the ability to translate complex financial information into executive-level recommendations.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with experience preparing executive summaries, governance materials, and committee reporting.
  • The ability to influence senior stakeholders and challenge assumptions constructively.
  • Demonstrated leadership of finance professionals and cross-functional initiatives.
  • High attention to detail, with strong organizational, documentation, and project management skills.
  • Experience managing hybrid or remote teams (preferred).
  • Ability to work in the office up to 2 days per week.

Experience and education

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in insurance finance, reinsurance, FP&A, treasury, collateral management, program business, or financial analysis.
  • Experience supporting MGA or delegated authority business (strongly preferred).
  • Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, profitability analysis, executive reporting, and financial governance.
  • Experience reviewing reinsurance agreements, collateral structures, financial controls, and insurance program performance.
  • Experience presenting financial recommendations to executive leadership, committees, auditors, regulators, and external stakeholders (preferred).

job.title: Senior Payroll & Benefits Administrator
job.description:
Senior Payroll & Benefits Administrator

Job Requirements:

  • Minimum 4 years of payroll, benefits administration, accounting operations or related experience; experience with executive benefit or non-qualified benefit plans desired
  • Undergraduate degree in Accounting, Finance, Human Resources, Business Administration or related field preferred or equivalent payroll, benefits or accounting experience
  • Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) desired
  • Working knowledge of payroll and benefit accounting concepts, reconciliations, journal entries, payment processing and supporting documentation
  • Applied knowledge of state and federal regulations pertaining to payroll
  • Experience with Workday Financials or Workday HCM, UltiPro/UKG, or similar payroll, HRIS or financial systems desired
  • Strong analytical, organizational and follow-up skills with excellent attention to detail and ability to manage recurring deadlines
  • Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive compensation, benefits, employee, executive and retiree information with discretion and confidentiality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to coordinate effectively with Accounting, Human Resources, Legal, Payroll, external vendors and auditors
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; Specifically Excel, Word, and Outlook
  • Ability to maintain accurate schedules, reconciliations and records

 

Core Competencies:

  • Collaborative Communications and Behavior: Develops and maintains effective working relationships as a team member and across divisions; readily collaborates and shares information, seeks and provides constructive feedback, and supports a respectful workplace
  • Initiative and Accountability: Proactively addresses opportunities to enhance the firm’s people, processes, products, and services, takes ownership for one’s responsibilities by acting with integrity and in the best interest of the organization and stakeholders
  • Quality-Focused: Demonstrates a solution-focus, displays thoroughness and accuracy through quality deliverables, and demonstrates persistence and perseverance in achieving concrete and tangible outcomes
  • Service-Oriented: Conveys a genuine desire and ability to anticipate and meet customer needs and creates and nurtures mutually beneficial relationships within the firm and with firm members and brokers

 

Essential Job Functions:

Data Management and Reporting

  • Prepare and maintain recurring schedules, reconciliations and supporting analyses for payroll, benefits, pension, SERP, COLI and other executive benefit-related accounting activities
  • Assist with monthly payroll and benefit accounting entries, research reconciliation differences and prepare support for manager review
  • Support annual and recurring benefit plan valuation, audit and reporting processes by compiling census, compensation, account balance, payout and plan information for vendors, auditors and internal stakeholders
  • Maintain assigned participant, payout, policy, account and payment tracking reports related to SERP, frozen Option Plan, COLI, AYCO financial counseling and other benefit programs administered through Accounting

Communication and Documentation

  • Coordinate documentation and support for COLI policy payments, policy value reporting, death benefit claims and accounting tax reporting support, including preparation of required forms and correspondence for review
  • Prepare, compile and/or route Workday payment requests, payroll gross-up support, invoice documentation, vendor payment support, e-signature requests and related accounting documentation, subject to required approvals
  • Assist with vendor coordination and information exchange involving benefit plan providers, payroll vendors, auditors and internal stakeholders like Human Resources; maintain accurate contact lists and historical documentation

The client and the opportunity

Our client is the U.S. specialty insurance platform of a large international insurance group, backed by the group's global capital and data capabilities. The platform is in build mode, and this is a founding leadership seat. The client is named under NDA once mutual interest is established.


The Head of Data Engineering owns the enterprise data strategy and the design, build, and operation of the entire data ecosystem. Every underwriting decision, pricing model, claim outcome, regulatory filing, and dollar reported to the parent group depends on this platform. The leader sets the data agenda, owns it end to end, and is accountable at the executive level, building with leverage rather than headcount across group data teams, a strategic cloud data partnership, and contracted vendor teams.


What you'll own

  • Strategy and architecture. How data is captured, modeled, governed, and distributed, plus the canonical data model for policy, claim, billing, and financial data, enforced across all vendor platforms with authority to accept or reject integrations.
  • The platform, greenfield to production. Kafka event ingestion, a Snowflake analytics hub, dbt transformation layers, and the semantic and reporting layers above them, with reliability, scalability, and cost owned as a production operation.
  • Bordereaux automation. Ingestion, validation, and reconciliation across MGA programs, TPA claims feeds, and reinsurer reporting.
  • Financial and regulatory data. One transaction-level spine serving US GAAP, US Statutory, and IFRS 17, plus the data behind statutory filings, NAIC reporting, AM Best submissions, and state examinations.
  • Governance, analytics, and AI enablement. Ownership, stewardship, lineage, quality, and access control enforced in the architecture, including NYDFS Part 500 and state privacy obligations, and the data foundation under every analytics and AI capability.
  • Extended team and group relationships. A leveraged delivery model across group engineering and vendor partners, and the data relationship with group finance, actuarial, and technology leadership overseas.


What the client is looking for

  • 10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or enterprise data platform leadership, with accountability for production platforms at scale.
  • Deep hands-on command of Snowflake, dbt, and event streaming such as Kafka.
  • Enterprise builds taken greenfield to production, directing vendor delivery teams.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. excess and surplus specialty products and underwriting dynamics.
  • Bachelor's in a quantitative discipline. Preferred: P&C data structures, multi-framework reporting, cloud data certifications, MBA.
  • Executive presence with senior stakeholders and board-level audiences.


What you'll gain

  • Founding ownership of the data strategy for a new specialty platform, with executive visibility.
  • Competitive compensation, executive incentive, and long-term incentive eligibility.
  • Hybrid working, with travel up to 25% for leadership, planning, and client engagements.
  • Comprehensive health, wellness, retirement, and financial wellbeing programs.
